verdict.rationale: The Wally CLI runs local models offline and also lets users choose RunAnywhere's own hosted cloud models through the same tools, for example with the `--cloud` flag, so hosted and local execution share one interface. The only cloud backend evidenced is RunAnywhere's first-party hosted service, not third-party cloud AI providers. missing for 10: connecting third-party cloud providers (e.g., OpenAI or Anthropic keys) alongside local models, evidence of mixing providers within one session or UI, independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a power-user, I can connect to cloud AI providers alongside local models within the same interface

citations.quote: Cloud models run on RunAnywhere's hardware instead of the user's, so you can use models too large for a laptop while keeping the same tools.
When a small model on your own machine is enough, the same CLI runs it, offline and without an account.
`--cloud` is an `opencode` flag: it asks for the hosted model rather than one on this machine.
Hosted and local execution are explicit choices. Wally does not silently move a request between them.
